evidence.methodology_note: Packet-only worker for Assigned languages=[Swift] under ecosystem metrics metric.implemented_platform_coverage and metric.external_integration_coverage. Only the Swift language key is populated; the runner is expected to merge disjoint per-language shards. Rubrics below are declared as frozen, reproducible, and intended to be applied identically to every language.

metric.external_integration_coverage.limitations: External integration breadth was assessed via a fixed 10-domain checklist rather than exhaustive package-index enumeration; per-domain scores rely on a small number of representative, officially-documented or clearly first-party/workgroup-affiliated projects (AWS SDK for Swift, PostgresNIO/PostgresKit, mongo-swift-driver, swift-kafka-client, grpc-swift, Fluent, Vapor/Hummingbird) rather than a full census of the Swift Package Index. A community source explicitly frames the overall ecosystem as smaller than JavaScript's npm ecosystem, which is reflected in middling (2/3) scores for less-graduated domains such as messaging, observability, and container orchestration.
metric.external_integration_coverage.rubric: Ten fixed external-integration domains are checked for Swift, each scored 0-3 (0=no working integration; 1=unmaintained/fragile community-only library; 2=actively maintained community or single-vendor library, or an incubating official workgroup project; 3=official/vendor-backed or workgroup-graduated, production-grade, multi-consumer integration). Domains: (1) major cloud provider SDK, (2) relational/SQL database driver, (3) NoSQL database driver, (4) message queue/streaming client, (5) gRPC/Protobuf RPC, (6) ORM, (7) web framework, (8) observability (metrics/tracing), (9) container/orchestration client, (10) CI/CD and package registry integration. Final score = (sum of domain scores / 30) * 100.

swift_domain_findings.basis: AWS SDK for Swift reached general availability and is production-ready and cross-platform, but Microsoft's official Azure SDK for iOS has long remained in beta and not recommended for production, and Google Cloud lacks an equivalent first-party idiomatic Swift SDK, so multi-cloud coverage is uneven.
citations: result 14-1,14-2: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the AWS SDK for Swift...Customers can now use AWS SDK for Swift for production workloads.

result 14-3: AWS SDK for Swift provides a modern, user-friendly, and native Swift interface for accessing Amazon Web Services from Apple platforms, AWS Lambda, and Linux-based Swift on Server applications.
result 45-1,45-3: Note: The SDK is currently in beta...We do not currently recommend them for production use.

swift_domain_findings.basis: PostgresNIO/PostgresKit and MySQL drivers are mature, non-blocking, SwiftNIO-based packages maintained under the Vapor/Swift Server ecosystem.
citations: result 24-9,24-10: PostgresKit supports building and serializing Postgres-dialect SQL queries using SQLKit's API...PostgresKit uses PostgresNIO to connect and communicate with the database server asynchronously.
result 25-5: Fluent 4 comes with multiple database driver implementations, this means that you can easily replace the recommended PostgreSQL driver with SQLite, MySQL or MongoDB.

swift_domain_findings.basis: MongoDB provides an official first-party Swift driver plus a Vapor integration, alongside community options.
citations: result 23-11: MongoDB maintains an official client, mongo-swift-driver, along with a Vapor integration, mongodb-vapor.
result 26-13: MongoKitten is a fast, pure Swift MongoDB driver built for Server Side Swift.

swift_domain_findings.basis: A Kafka client exists under the swift-server GitHub organization (Swift Server Workgroup), indicating organized but still-incubating support rather than a long-graduated, universally adopted client.
citations: result 28-1: Contribute to swift-server/swift-kafka-client development by creating an account on GitHub.
result 19-1: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Oracle, Redis, MongoDB, Apache Cassandra, Apache Kafka -- all non-blocking, built on SwiftNIO.

swift_domain_findings.basis: grpc-swift is a long-running, actively maintained implementation hosted directly under the official grpc GitHub organization, graduated within the Swift Server Workgroup, and builds across iOS, macOS, visionOS, watchOS, tvOS, Linux, Wasm, and Android.
citations: result 34-4: iOS, macOS, visionOS, watchOS, tvOS, Linux, Wasm, Android...View on GitHub...Member of the SSWG Graduated collection.
result 34-2: In development for 9 years, with 1,986 commits and 101 releases.
result 37-3: grpc grpc-haskell grpc-java grpc-go grpc-swift grpc-node.

swift_domain_findings.basis: Fluent is a mature, official Vapor-ecosystem ORM with multiple database backends (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB), documented directly on swift.org's server packages page.
citations: result 26-2,26-10: Fluent helps you work with databases, providing a high-level, type-safe API for querying and manipulating data in Vapor apps.
result 23-1: Fluent is an ORM framework for Swift. It takes advantage of Swift's strong type system to provide an easy-to-use interface for your database.

swift_domain_findings.basis: Vapor and Hummingbird are mature, actively maintained server frameworks officially listed on swift.org's package ecosystem page.
citations: result 26-4: Vapor is an HTTP web framework for Swift, providing an expressive and easy-to-use foundation for websites, APIs, and cloud projects.
result 26-8: Hummingbird is a lightweight, flexible server framework written in Swift.

swift_domain_findings.basis: Swift's server ecosystem exposes standard logging/metrics/tracing APIs pluggable into Prometheus and Jaeger, but this is via community/workgroup backends rather than a single dominant vendor-graded product.
citations: result 19-3,19-4: Logging, Metrics, and Distributed Tracing -- all using Swift's standard APIs. Plug in Prometheus, Jaeger, or whatever your team uses.

swift_domain_findings.basis: Official Swift Docker images exist and the ecosystem documents cloud/container deployment, but a first-party, widely-graduated Kubernetes client comparable to Go's client-go is not established; coverage relies on community packages.
citations: result 26-1,26-9: It consists of an HTTP server, a web application framework, and extension modules...Hummingbird is a lightweight, flexible server framework written in Swift.

swift_domain_findings.basis: Swift Package Manager integrates with GitHub-hosted package indexes and CI systems, and Swift 6.4 standardized building across CI platforms via Swift Build, but the registry/tooling ecosystem is smaller and less centralized than more mature package registries.
citations: result 9-10: This standardization provides a unified build experience across integrated development environments and continuous integration platforms, enabling Swift packages to build and run full test suites on macOS, iOS, Linux and Windows.
result 19-6,19-7,19-8: Is this ecosystem as large as npm? No. Not even in the same universe.

corroborating_evidence: result 2-1,2-2: Although Swift serves as Apple's primary language for macOS and iOS application development, the open-source community continues to expand its reach, and Tuesday's Swift 6.4 release continued that work.

result 3-1,3-2: Since it was first open-sourced in 2015, Swift has grown from a language focused on creating apps for Darwin-based systems into a cross-platform development language supporting Linux, Windows, and various embedded systems.

result 4-4: Android support arrives through the Android NDK 30 toolchain, a pairing that positions Swift as the first Apple-originated language with official cross-platform reach that includes Google's mobile ecosystem.

result 9-10: This standardization provides a unified build experience across integrated development environments and continuous integration platforms, enabling Swift packages to build and run full test suites on macOS, iOS, Linux and Windows.
metric.implemented_platform_coverage.limitations: Android support is very recent (GA reported around Swift 6.3/6.4 in 2026) and community sources note tooling maturity gaps, e.g. result 5-8: it is not yet fully integrated with Android Studio, and command-line building skills are essential. This is treated as a maturity caveat rather than a category miss, since the SDK is officially shipped by swift.org.
metric.implemented_platform_coverage.rubric: Ten officially-documented/first-party-supported platform-target categories are checked from the language's own official distribution/toolchain documentation (not third-party ports or unofficial community forks): (1) primary vendor desktop OS, (2) Linux (multi-distro official binaries), (3) Windows, (4) primary mobile OS, (5) secondary mobile OS, (6) WebAssembly, (7) embedded/bare-metal/microcontroller, (8) server-side/cloud deployment tooling (official container images or server workgroup), (9) other same-vendor OS variants, (10) an additional BSD/Unix variant. Each category present in official docs = 1 point; category unsupported or community-only = 0 points. Score = (categories met / 10) * 100.

swift_category_findings.basis: Native, first-party Apple platform; Xcode/toolchain ships with macOS support by default.

swift_category_findings.citation: result 1-1: Linux includes Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Amazon Linux and Red Hat Universal Base Image platforms.
result 5-1: Windows users can directly obtain it through the installation package, and Linux and macOS users can also download it separately.
result 7-1: The Swift SDK for Android is available today, bundled with the Windows installer or downloadable separately for use on Linux or macOS.
result 9-14: The Wasm SDK is available directly from the Swift.org install.
result 9-6: Swift's reach expands with deeper language interoperability, including... Embedded Swift for microcontrollers.
result 26-3: Swift has several mature back-end frameworks, ORM, database connection packages, and more.

swift_category_findings.basis: Native, first-party Apple platforms shipped with every Swift toolchain release; confirmed as build targets for major Swift packages (e.g. result 34-4 lists iOS, macOS, visionOS, watchOS, tvOS, Linux, Wasm, Android as grpc-swift build targets).

The official swift.org platform-support page enumerates only Linux distributions, Windows, Apple platforms, and Android; FreeBSD/other BSDs are community-maintained forks, not part of the official platform-support matrix (result 1-1).
